correctness.rationale: The affine centered eigenvector gives a universal Rayleigh bound and the exactly diagonalized parabolic weighted path gives a rigid baseline. First-order simple-eigenvalue perturbation shows strict activation below price (n−1)^2. At equality the eigenvector equations force the affine one-dimensional family; the exact covariance C of centered path cumulative sums maps the full PSD constraint to A_n−δ((n−1)I−J)⪰0, so the endpoint is λ2(A_n)/(n−1). Every nonstandard identity was derived in the proof and checked in exact rational finite cases: VERIFY_OK 200 assertion groups. Boundaries n≥3, δ=0, δ=ρ and all real B>0 are treated; no conclusion for the full subcritical optimal allocation is claimed.

value.rationale: In a natural budgeted diffusion network-design problem, the theorem decides exactly when one costly optional cycle link is always used, forbidden, or variably active among optimizers. The complete positive-dimensional critical face and its sharp spectral cutoff in an auxiliary Brownian-bridge complete graph reveal an otherwise hidden structural stability and eigenvalue multiplicity change; the result is not a mere path renaming or another unevaluated SDP restatement.
